# FABLE review — thin skills/Behavior design (v1)

**Method:** scenario review against `origin/main` @ `30a4bd836`. Read-only. No code changes proposed
beyond the four must-fixes in §5.

---

## Context

The locked v1 design makes four bets: skills become instruction text only (nixPackages move to agent
`nixConfig` / connector `agentTooling`); skills stay in `agents.skills_config` jsonb; Behavior stays
the automation unit; and a Behavior may optionally "use a skill" by **copying the skill body into
`watcher_versions.prompt`** at save/apply. No skill entity, no skill versions, no skill-owned
sources/reactions/schema.

This review grounds each claim in code and walks 12 fables to find where the copy-on-expand model
breaks.

---

## 1. Executive verdict

The thin design is **directionally right and mostly already true in the code** — skills have been
narrowing for months (network + MCP config removed, guardrails removed in #2290, catalog manifests
never emitted packages), and Behavior already owns triggers, sources, classifiers, reactions, and a
pinned-per-run version. Item 1 (strip nixPackages) and items 2/3/5/6/7 are safe. The one genuinely
new mechanism — item 4/8, copying a skill body into `watcher_versions.prompt` — has **three
mechanical defects that make it fail as specified**, none of which require the heavier
pin-snapshot/entity-skills design to fix. The worst is that the design's own rule ("do not rely on
`cat .skills` for Behavior runs") is *unenforceable today*: `session-runner.ts` writes live skill
bodies into `.skills/` on **every** session including Behavior runs, and `instruction-service` tells
the agent to `cat` them — so a "frozen" prompt copy and the live skill body coexist inside the same
turn and the model picks. Verdict: **GO with four must-fixes**, and split item 1 into its own PR
because it is the only part with a live-rollout hazard.

---

## 2. Duplication map

| # | The same data lives in | Intentional? | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Live skill body** (`skills_config[].content`) ↔ **frozen copy** (`watcher_versions.prompt`) | Yes — the design *is* the copy | Medium on its own |
| D2 | **`.skills/<name>/SKILL.md` written live per run** (`session-runner.ts:727-763`) ↔ D1's frozen copy, **inside the same turn** | **No** — nobody designed this; it falls out of the existing sync | **HIGH** |
| D3 | Behavior prompt-source pickers: `CreationMode = "template" \| "scratch" \| "clone"` (`create-watcher-form.tsx:22`) — all three already write `prompt`. `BEHAVIOR_CATALOG_TEMPLATES` (`catalog/behavior-templates.ts`) is *already* a prompt library. "Use skill" is a 4th source writing the same field. | No | Medium (product) |
| D4 | Skill nix unioned **twice**: apply-time bake (`map-config.ts:295-305`) + runtime union (`platform-helpers.ts:100-127`) | No — a known 2-impl overlap | Medium; **item 1 deletes it — a real win** |
| D5 | Five skill shapes: `SkillConfigSchema` (core), `Skill` in `api-types.ts:27-39` (has a phantom `permissions` with no producer/consumer), CLI `interface Skill` (`define.ts:586-618`), `SkillEditorRow` (owletto), `AgentConfig.skills` (`gateway/config/index.ts:76-79`) | No | Medium; pre-existing, but item 1 must edit all of them |
| D6 | `SkillConfig.content` (full body) ↔ `SkillConfig.instructions` (short override, rendered as `→ …` in the index) | Partly | Low — but "copy the skill body" is **ambiguous between them**; pick one explicitly |
| D7 | Skill `modelPreference` / `thinkingLevel` (advisory prompt text) ↔ `watchers.execution_config.model` (structural) | Yes | Low — but a body-copy silently drops both |

**Drift severity overall: HIGH, and it is D2, not D1.** D1 (library-vs-automation drift across time)
is a legitimate product choice and is already auditable — `runs.run_metadata.prompt_rendered`
(`behavior-mode.ts:587-607`) records the exact text every run used. D2 is drift *within one turn*,
which no user can reason about and no audit surfaces.

---

## 3. Fable results

Owner columns: **when** = who decides the automation fires; **what** = who owns the instruction text;
**tools** = who supplies binaries/creds; **data** = who owns sources/schema.

| # | Fable | when / what / tools / data | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | One-off automation, typed prompt | Behavior / Behavior / agent+connector / Behavior | **PASS** — unchanged path, no skill in the loop |
| F2 | PR-review skill + GitHub `agentTooling` | Behavior / skill body copy / **connector** (`resolver.ts` → `deployment-manager.ts:1638-1670` mints `gh`, `GH_TOKEN` lease, domains) / Behavior | **PASS on the premise** — `gh` never came from the skill, so item 1 costs nothing here. Two live caveats: declared `git` is still 127 (`UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS`), so "open the PR" is half-blocked; remote Vercel sandboxes install packages via `nix profile install` (`runtime/providers/vercel.ts:348-431`) — confirm that path still receives the connector union |
| F3 | Two Behaviors, one skill file | each Behavior / two independent copies / — / — | **FAIL-SOFT** — with no stored ref, nothing joins them. Same-`watcher_group_id` behaviors share one version chain; different groups get two copies that must each be re-expanded. No "which Behaviors use this skill" is answerable |
| F4 | Edit skill in git → `lobu apply` | apply / re-expanded body / — / — | **PASS, conditional.** Needs (a) a `skill` field on the CLI `Behavior` (`define.ts:398-451`), (b) expansion in `map-config` **before** `diffWatcher`, (c) **byte-stable expansion** — frontmatter stripping and trailing-newline handling must be deterministic or every `apply` bumps a version for free |
| F5 | Edit skill in UI, expect automations to change | — | **FAIL by design, then FAILS WORSE.** `saveSkills` → `PATCH /agents/:id/config` touches only `skills_config`; no re-expansion. But the next Behavior run syncs the **new** body to `.skills/` and the system prompt still says "read the full skill instructions: `cat .skills/*/SKILL.md`". The user gets a *partial* change with no way to predict which half applied |
| F6 | Chat uses latest skill, automation uses old copy | — | **FAIL as specified.** The intent is defensible; the mechanism doesn't hold. The automation turn contains both texts (D2). The design says "do NOT rely on `cat .skills` for Behavior runs" — that is a wish, not an enforcement point |
| F7 | Reaction-heavy Behavior, thin prompt | Behavior / Behavior / — / Behavior | **PASS.** `reactions_guidance` is version-bound and appended to `prompt_rendered` after render (`behavior-mode.ts:564-573`). A skill body composes cleanly. Item 7 (skills never own reactions) is correct |
| F8 | Entity type / schema change | org / — / — / org | **PASS, one edge.** Orthogonal as claimed. But `create_version` runs `assertKeyingConfigEntityTypeExists` + `assertWatcherSourcesResolve`; a routine skill-driven bump therefore re-validates keying against the *current* org schema and can fail for a reason unrelated to the skill edit |
| F9 | Mid-run WAIT + apply bumps version | run pins version / **split** | **PASS for prompt, FAIL for skills.** The run snapshots `version_id` into `approved_input` (`automation.ts:148-177, 301-304`; asserted by `watchers/group-edit.test.ts`). The resumed turn re-fetches `/worker/session-context` and re-syncs `.skills` from **live** settings — pinned prompt, unpinned skill body. Same root cause as F5/F6 |
| F10 | Catalog skill upgrade | — | **FAIL (pre-existing).** `mergeSkillInstalledWithCatalog` skips the catalog entry outright when the id is installed — no version compare — and `generateSkillsManifest` hardcodes `version: "1.0.0"`. There is no upgrade path *today*, before this design. Under the design an upgrade would need to write `skills_config` **and** re-expand N Behavior prompts; neither exists |
| F11 | Skill body contains `{{…}}` | — | **FAIL — hard.** `watcher_versions.prompt` is a Handlebars template: `renderPromptTemplate` does `hbs.compile(template, {noEscape:true})` with **no try/catch** (`template-renderer.ts:119-122`). A skill documenting templating, a JSON example with mustaches, or any `{{#if}}`/`{{#each}}` snippet either renders to empty (silent) or **throws inside `get_content` behavior-mode and kills the run** |
| F12 | Rollout of item 1 (strip nixPackages) | — | **FAIL without a backfill.** `platform-finance`-style agents whose only nix source is a skill lose their binaries at the next deploy, surfacing as exit 127 at run time. `examples/sales/skills/account-brief/SKILL.md:4` ships `nixPackages: [jq]`; `docs/SECURITY.md:18,27,29,87` and the CLI README template teach it; `tool-policy.ts` error text literally says "declare it in nixPackages instead". Prod blast radius is small (2 skill rows org-wide) but the docs/examples surface is not |

**Bonus, low severity:** `extractSourcesFromPromptTokens` scans the prompt for
`@[kind:id:label](path)` tokens and turns them into `version_sources`. The regex is structured
enough that ordinary markdown won't trip it, but a pasted body containing that exact link shape would
silently mint a Behavior source. Worth one test, not a blocker.

---

## 4. What is already true (don't rebuild it)

- **Run provenance exists.** `runs.run_metadata.prompt_rendered` stores the exact rendered prompt per
  run (`behavior-mode.ts:587-607`, read by `watcher-run-thread.ts:91`). That is the audit trail item 5
  says it doesn't need to invent.
- **Version pinning exists** and survives mid-run edits (`automation.ts`, `group-edit.test.ts`).
- **Prompt libraries exist.** `BEHAVIOR_CATALOG_TEMPLATES` + `CreationMode: template|scratch|clone`.
- **Skills already never own tools in the catalog.** `generateSkillsManifest` emits only
  `{instructions, hidden}` — bundled skills (`skills/lobu`, `skills/lobu-operator`) declare zero
  packages. Item 1 formalizes what the catalog already does.
- **Connector `agentTooling` already covers the F2 case** end to end, packages + lease + domains.

---

## 5. Must-fix before ship

**M1 — Stop `.skills` from contradicting the frozen prompt in a Behavior run.** (fixes F5, F6, F9;
kills D2.) `session-runner.ts:727-763` writes live bodies unconditionally. Either skip the `.skills`
sync + the skills index for behavior-run sessions, or sync the pinned content. Without this, item 4's
central rule is advisory and the whole freeze story is false. Cheapest correct form: gate the sync on
run kind.

**M2 — Neutralize the copied body against Handlebars.** (fixes F11.) `hbs.compile` is uncaught. Wrap
the copied region in a Handlebars raw block, or escape mustaches at copy time. A run that dies on a
skill's `{{#each}}` example is an unacceptable first-week bug.

**M3 — Store the skill ref + content hash.** (fixes F3, F4, F10; enables the "which Behaviors use
this?" answer.) One nullable field is enough, and `watchers.execution_config` jsonb already exists so
it needs no migration. Without a ref there is no re-expansion target for UI-created Behaviors, no
catalog-upgrade path, and no join. This is also the "stamp resolved-skill provenance (name + content
hash) into run records" item already on the composition roadmap — same field, two payoffs.

**M4 — Backfill + docs for the nixPackages strip.** (fixes F12.) One-time move of
`skills_config[].nixPackages` into `agents.nix_config.packages`, then update `docs/SECURITY.md`,
`examples/sales/skills/account-brief/SKILL.md`, `examples/personal-finance/*`, the CLI README
template, and the `tool-policy.ts` hint text. Deleting the schema field alone is a silent
capability regression.

### Accept as known limits

- **Library-vs-automation drift across time (D1).** Correct call; `prompt_rendered` makes it
  auditable. Document it in the "Use skill" UI copy in one line.
- **No skill version product (item 5).** Correct. Git + `lobu apply` is the human axis; `create_version`
  is the machine axis. Nothing to build.
- **`modelPreference` / `thinkingLevel` don't survive a body copy (D7).** Fine for v1 — say so; the
  structural override lives at `watchers.execution_config.model`.
- **F8's create_version re-validation edge.** Real but rare; leave it.
- **`git` still exits 127 for connector-tooling agents.** Pre-existing, tracked separately, out of scope.

---

## 6. What NOT to build

- **No skills table, no `$skill` entity.** Shelved on prod data (2 skill rows, duplication factor 1.00);
  the `$` prefix would hide it from the entity rail and the generic board cannot author markdown.
- **No skill version history / semver / diff UI.** M3's content hash is the entire versioning need.
- **No per-Behavior skill *restriction*.** The server has none today; don't invent an authz surface.
- **No 4th picker UI.** "Use skill" should be a new mode inside the existing `CreationMode` switch and
  the existing `CatalogPicker`, not a parallel component — otherwise D3 gets worse.
- **No `nix_packages` on `BehaviorExecutionConfig`** (the old Stage 2 idea). No demonstrated need.
- **No "sync from skill" refresh button in v1.** Re-expand at save/apply; that's it.
- **Don't touch `modelPreference` / `thinkingLevel` in this pass** — orthogonal, and removing them is
  a separate argument.

---

## 7. Sequencing note (one branch = one concern)

Item 1 and items 4/8 are independent and have opposite risk profiles. Split:

- **PR1 — strip nixPackages** (+ M4 backfill/docs). Touches core contract, CLI apply, platform-helpers,
  owletto skill editor, docs, examples. This is the only part with a live-rollout hazard.
- **PR2 — "Use skill" on Behavior** (+ M1, M2, M3). Pure addition; no existing run changes shape.

One caveat on PR1 worth writing down rather than silently contradicting: the 2026-07-27 memo rejected
moving nix off skills. Its ground was "moving nix to *Behavior* breaks skills used in chat, where no
behavior is in the loop." This design moves nix to **agent `nixConfig`**, which is in scope for chat
too — so the objection does not apply. Update that memo when PR1 lands; don't leave two contradictory
records.

---

## 8. Go / No-go

**GO** on the thin design. It is the right shape, and it is closer to the code's current direction
than the heavier alternative. Ship it as two PRs with M1–M4 in scope. Do not escalate to pin-snapshot
columns, entity skills, or dual task/method fields — none of the twelve fables needs them; every
failure above is mechanical and locally fixable.

**Confidence: 82 / 100.**
Basis: I read the actual code for every claim above — `SkillConfigSchema`, `instruction-service`
skills provider, the `.skills` sync in `session-runner.ts`, `template-renderer.ts` (the Handlebars
throw), `extractSourcesFromPromptTokens`, `create_version` + watcher-group semantics, catalog
merge/generation, `map-config` nix baking, and the `CreationMode` switch — from `origin/main`, not the
local tree. Not verified: prod counts of Behaviors that would need re-expansion (no DB access this
session); whether `.skills` reaches the remote Vercel sandbox filesystem; whether any customer skill
today carries `nixPackages` beyond the shipped example.

**Next actions**

1. Decide M1's form — suppress `.skills` for behavior runs, or sync pinned content. This is the one
   choice that changes PR2's shape.
2. Confirm M3's storage — `watchers.execution_config` jsonb (no migration) vs a real column.
3. Run a read-only prod audit: how many `skills_config[]` entries carry `nixPackages`, and how many
   agents have skill-only nix. Sizes M4's backfill.
4. Write the F11 reproducer first (a skill body with `{{#each x}}` → Behavior run) — it is the cheapest
   red test in the set and it proves the copy path before any of it is built.

- **Prompt libraries exist.** `BEHAVIOR_CATALOG_TEMPLATES` + `CreationMode: template|scratch|clone`.

central rule is advisory and the whole freeze story is false. Cheapest correct form: gate the sync on
run kind.

**M2 — Neutralize the copied body against Handlebars.** (fixes F11.) `hbs.compile` is uncaught. Wrap
the copied region in a Handlebars raw block, or escape mustaches at copy time. A run that dies on a
skill's `{{#each}}` example is an unacceptable first-week bug.

- **F8's create_version re-validation edge.** Real but rare; leave it.
- **`git` still exits 127 for connector-tooling agents.** Pre-existing, tracked separately, out of scope.

- **No skills table, no `$skill` entity.** Shelved on prod data (2 skill rows, duplication factor 1.00);

# Implications for "Behavior uses a skill" (copy skill body into `watcher_versions.prompt`)

Things the design has to reckon with, ranked by risk:

1. **Skills today are agent-scoped, not behavior-scoped.** `SkillConfigSchema` at `/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/core/src/contracts/agent-settings.ts:118-129` has `{ repo, name, description, instructions, enabled, system, content, nixPackages, modelPreference, thinkingLevel }`, stored in `agents.settings.skillsConfig`. CLI loads them from the agent dir: `packages/cli/src/commands/_lib/apply/map-config.ts:282-292` (`mergeAgentDirArtifacts`) and `desired-state.ts:338`. There is currently **no link at all** from a Behavior to a skill. Copying `skill.content` into `watcher_versions.prompt` flattens an agent-level artifact into a behavior-level version — the provenance ("which skill, which revision") has nowhere to live: the closest columns are `change_notes` (free text) and `description`.

2. **The prompt is Handlebars-compiled, not plain text.** `validateTemplate` (`packages/server/src/watchers/renderer.ts:12-28`) runs `Handlebars.precompile` and a failure is a hard 422 at save. Skill bodies (SKILL.md) routinely contain `{{ }}`, `{{#...}}`, and code fences. A skill body with mustaches will either fail to save or silently render to empty at run time (`noEscape: true`, unknown vars → `""`). This is the single biggest correctness hazard.

3. **`@[kind:id:label](path)` tokens in the prompt auto-derive `sources[]`.** `packages/server/src/watchers/source-refs.ts:165` (`PROMPT_REF_TOKEN`) + `:201` `extractSourcesFromPromptTokens`. And in `handleCreateVersion` (`version-actions.ts:90-121`), *any* `args.prompt !== undefined` sets `promptEdited = true`, which changes source semantics. So a skill-body paste that happens to contain a markdown link after an `@` can inject or clobber sources; and even a benign paste flips the "prompt edited" branch, which combined with the previous prompt having tokens will **re-derive sources from scratch** and can drop existing ones (surfaced as `removed_sources` in the response, `version-actions.ts:322-330`).

4. **No idempotence guard.** Re-applying the same skill body produces a fresh version row every time on the server; only the CLI's `diffWatcher` string compare (`diff.ts:533`) prevents churn. Any non-CLI path (MCP, SDK, UI, approval re-run) that "applies a skill" needs its own no-op check, or version numbers will inflate. Consider adding a server-side "identical to current version → return existing" short-circuit, or a `source_skill` + content-hash column.

5. **In-flight runs won't see the new body, but a queued run may block a re-pin.** The pin is correct and deliberate (`queue-service.ts:441`), but `findActiveWatcherRun` reuse (`:433`) means "apply skill then trigger" can silently execute the OLD body. If "apply a skill" is meant to take effect immediately, that reuse path needs an explicit answer.

6. **Version-bound vs row-bound split is asymmetric.** If a skill also wants to contribute a reaction script or sources, those are NOT in `watcher_versions` — reaction script is unversioned on `watchers`, `version_sources` is always NULL. A "skill" that bundles prompt + sources + reaction script would be applied through three different write paths (`create_version`, `create_version` per-assignment UPDATE, `set_reaction_script`) with no atomicity across them.

7. **Approval path re-runs args verbatim.** `ManageBehaviorsProposal` (`manage-behaviors.ts:893-895`) — a pending `create_version` carrying a skill body approved days later will clobber whatever version landed in between. If skills are applied by agents (non-human principals), this is the default path.

8. **Size.** `prompt` is unbounded `text` and there is no length validation anywhere. Full skill bodies will inflate every `watcher_versions` row plus every `runs.run_metadata.prompt_rendered` copy (`behavior-mode.ts:587`). The markdown formatter already truncates at 1000 chars (`markdown-formatter.ts:1173`).

# Data flow summary

```
config file / MCP / UI
   │
   ├─ create ──────► crud.ts handleCreate ──► INSERT watchers + watcher_versions(v1)
   │                                          └─ watchers.current_version_id = v1
   │
   ├─ update ──────► crud.ts handleUpdate ──► UPDATE watchers (scalar only;
   │                                          name/description/prompt/sources REJECTED)
   │
   └─ create_version ► version-actions.ts:33 ─► advisory lock(group)
                                              ├─ INSERT watcher_versions (version = MAX+1)
                                              ├─ UPDATE watchers ... WHERE watcher_group_id  (cascade)
                                              └─ UPDATE watchers ... WHERE id = behavior_id  (sources/schedule)

scheduler tick / event / manual trigger
   └─ createWatcherRun ─► SELECT watchers.current_version_id  ──► approved_input.version_id  (FROZEN)
        │                 (reuses an ACTIVE run if one exists — no re-pin!)
        └─ dispatch ─► getWatcherInstructions(versionId) → raw watcher_versions.prompt in the message
                       │
                       ├─ read_knowledge(template_version_id) ─► behavior-mode.ts
                       │     ├─ renderPromptTemplate(version.prompt, {entities, content, sources})
                       │     ├─ + Pagination / Reactions Guidance / past reactions / past feedback
                       │     └─ UPDATE runs SET run_metadata.prompt_rendered = <enriched>
                       │
                       └─ completeWindow(template_version_id) ─► complete-window.ts (validates vs same version)
```

# Implications for "Behavior uses a skill" (copy skill body into `watcher_versions.prompt`)

Things the design has to reckon with, ranked by risk:

1. **Skills today are agent-scoped, not behavior-scoped.** `SkillConfigSchema` at `/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/core/src/contracts/agent-settings.ts:118-129` has `{ repo, name, description, instructions, enabled, system, content, nixPackages, modelPreference, thinkingLevel }`, stored in `agents.settings.skillsConfig`. CLI loads them from the agent dir: `packages/cli/src/commands/_lib/apply/map-config.ts:282-292` (`mergeAgentDirArtifacts`) and `desired-state.ts:338`. There is currently **no link at all** from a Behavior to a skill. Copying `skill.content` into `watcher_versions.prompt` flattens an agent-level artifact into a behavior-level version — the provenance ("which skill, which revision") has nowhere to live: the closest columns are `change_notes` (free text) and `description`.

2. **The prompt is Handlebars-compiled, not plain text.** `validateTemplate` (`packages/server/src/watchers/renderer.ts:12-28`) runs `Handlebars.precompile` and a failure is a hard 422 at save. Skill bodies (SKILL.md) routinely contain `{{ }}`, `{{#...}}`, and code fences. A skill body with mustaches will either fail to save or silently render to empty at run time (`noEscape: true`, unknown vars → `""`). This is the single biggest correctness hazard.

3. **`@[kind:id:label](path)` tokens in the prompt auto-derive `sources[]`.** `packages/server/src/watchers/source-refs.ts:165` (`PROMPT_REF_TOKEN`) + `:201` `extractSourcesFromPromptTokens`. And in `handleCreateVersion` (`version-actions.ts:90-121`), *any* `args.prompt !== undefined` sets `promptEdited = true`, which changes source semantics. So a skill-body paste that happens to contain a markdown link after an `@` can inject or clobber sources; and even a benign paste flips the "prompt edited" branch, which combined with the previous prompt having tokens will **re-derive sources from scratch** and can drop existing ones (surfaced as `removed_sources` in the response, `version-actions.ts:322-330`).

4. **No idempotence guard.** Re-applying the same skill body produces a fresh version row every time on the server; only the CLI's `diffWatcher` string compare (`diff.ts:533`) prevents churn. Any non-CLI path (MCP, SDK, UI, approval re-run) that "applies a skill" needs its own no-op check, or version numbers will inflate. Consider adding a server-side "identical to current version → return existing" short-circuit, or a `source_skill` + content-hash column.

5. **In-flight runs won't see the new body, but a queued run may block a re-pin.** The pin is correct and deliberate (`queue-service.ts:441`), but `findActiveWatcherRun` reuse (`:433`) means "apply skill then trigger" can silently execute the OLD body. If "apply a skill" is meant to take effect immediately, that reuse path needs an explicit answer.

6. **Version-bound vs row-bound split is asymmetric.** If a skill also wants to contribute a reaction script or sources, those are NOT in `watcher_versions` — reaction script is unversioned on `watchers`, `version_sources` is always NULL. A "skill" that bundles prompt + sources + reaction script would be applied through three different write paths (`create_version`, `create_version` per-assignment UPDATE, `set_reaction_script`) with no atomicity across them.

7. **Approval path re-runs args verbatim.** `ManageBehaviorsProposal` (`manage-behaviors.ts:893-895`) — a pending `create_version` carrying a skill body approved days later will clobber whatever version landed in between. If skills are applied by agents (non-human principals), this is the default path.

8. **Size.** `prompt` is unbounded `text` and there is no length validation anywhere. Full skill bodies will inflate every `watcher_versions` row plus every `runs.run_metadata.prompt_rendered` copy (`behavior-mode.ts:587`). The markdown formatter already truncates at 1000 chars (`markdown-formatter.ts:1173`).

content.text:
Review written to `/Users/burakemre/.claude/plans/architecture-review-request-snazzy-lightning.md` — duplication map §2, 15 fables §3, must-fixes §5, what-not-to-build §6.

**Executive verdict**

The thin design is right, and most of it is already true in the code: skills have been narrowing for months (network/MCP config gone, guardrails gone in #2290, bundled catalog manifests never emitted packages at all). Items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 are safe. The one genuinely new mechanism, copying a skill body into `watcher_versions.prompt`, has four mechanical defects that make it fail as specified. None of them need the heavier pin-snapshot/entity-skills design.

**The four that break it**

`watcher_versions.prompt` is a Handlebars template, not a text field. `validateTemplate` runs `Handlebars.precompile` at save (`watchers/renderer.ts:12-28`), so a SKILL.md containing a `{{#each}}` example is a hard 422 and simply cannot be attached; a well-formed but unknown `{{var}}` silently renders to empty at run time.

In `handleCreateVersion`, `promptEdited = args.prompt !== undefined` (`version-actions.ts:90`) alone flips source resolution to re-derive from prompt tokens. Attaching a skill body to a Behavior that had prompt-token sources drops them, reported as `removed_sources`. Invisible until the next run returns nothing.

The freeze isn't a freeze. `session-runner.ts:727-763` writes live skill bodies into `.skills/` on every session including Behavior runs, and `instruction-service` tells the agent to `cat` them. So the frozen prompt copy and the live skill body sit in the same turn and the model picks. That is what actually breaks the "edit skill in UI", "chat latest vs automation old", and "mid-run WAIT" fables, not drift across time.

There's no stored ref. Without one there's no re-expansion target for UI-created Behaviors, no join for "two Behaviors one skill", no catalog-upgrade path, and no idempotence guard (`handleCreateVersion` always inserts `MAX+1`). One field in the existing `watchers.execution_config` jsonb covers all four plus the run-provenance stamp already on the composition roadmap.

**Go / no-go: GO**, as two PRs. Strip nixPackages separately with a backfill, since it's the only part with a live-rollout hazard (`examples/sales/skills/account-brief/SKILL.md:4` ships `nixPackages: [jq]`, and `tool-policy.ts` error text tells agents to use it). Note it reverses the 2026-07-27 memo, though on different grounds: that memo rejected moving nix to *Behavior*; moving it to agent `nixConfig` keeps chat working.

One thing worth deciding early: if the stored ref is rejected, item 4 stops being a design item. `CreationMode = template | scratch | clone` already exists in `create-watcher-form.tsx:22` and all three prefill `prompt`; "Use skill" would just be a fourth entry in that picker.

**Confidence: 84.** Basis: every claim read from `origin/main` (local is 14 commits behind), including both Handlebars paths, the `.skills` sync, `handleCreateVersion`, run pinning in `queue-service.ts`, and catalog merge/generation. Not verified: prod counts (no DB access this session), whether `.skills` reaches the remote Vercel sandbox FS, and owletto's UI surface (read from the pinned submodule).

**Next actions**
1. Pick M1's form: suppress `.skills` for behavior runs, or sync pinned content. This is the choice that shapes PR2.
2. Decide the stored ref go/no-go, which decides whether item 4 is a feature or a picker entry.
3. Read-only prod audit of `skills_config[].nixPackages` to size the backfill.
4. Write the two red reproducers before building: skill body with `{{#each x}}`, and attaching a body to a Behavior with prompt-token sources.
